name: @smoothbricks/cowshed

wire-fixtures-test.//: Witness that cowshed:wire-fixtures publishes the corpus whole: cowshed:lint reads src/wire-fixtures.json while it regenerates, so a reader must see the old or the new formatted file, never the raw render.

options.command: cargo build --frozen -p cowshed-gateway --example ram_fixture -Z unstable-options --artifact-dir packages/cowshed/.cache/ram-fixture

wait-why.//: WAIT-WHY (specs/cowshed/05_gateway.md, Deadlines, Enforcement): clippy refuses the waits each crate's clippy.toml disallows; this refuses a kept one without an adjacent // WHY unbounded: that says what ends it. The note is not an option: nx:run-commands forwards every option it does not know to the command as an argument, and the check reads each argument as a crates directory.

build.//: Replaces the inferred build's native edges: build is the TypeScript library and its dependencies. The CLI is its own target, cli-native, the host's development build under .cache/bin/<platform> that the package launcher runs, so an ordinary build compiles no Rust; the shipping trees come from each platform target's production configuration.

refresh-harnesses.//: Cached on upstream vercel-labs/skills main, the revision the script reads, and on the script: generated.rs is its output.

cli-arm64-macos.//: outputDir is the tree this configuration writes: .cache/bin/<platform> by default, dist/bin/<platform> in production (specs/cowshed/06_cli.md, Launcher). One option feeds the declared output, napi's --output-dir and the receipt's --output, so the three cannot name different trees.

options.command: napi build --bin cowshed --target aarch64-apple-darwin --manifest-path crates/cowshed-cli/Cargo.toml --package cowshed-cli --output-dir {args.outputDir} && node "$(realpath ../../node_modules/@smoothbricks/nx-plugin)/../build-inputs/dist/ts/bin/smoo-nx-build-inputs.js" --manifest-path crates/cowshed-cli/Cargo.toml --dep-info aarch64-apple-darwin/debug/cowshed.d --output {args.outputDir}

production.command: napi build --release --bin cowshed --target aarch64-apple-darwin --manifest-path crates/cowshed-cli/Cargo.toml --package cowshed-cli --output-dir {args.outputDir} && node "$(realpath ../../node_modules/@smoothbricks/nx-plugin)/../build-inputs/dist/ts/bin/smoo-nx-build-inputs.js" --manifest-path crates/cowshed-cli/Cargo.toml --dep-info aarch64-apple-darwin/release/cowshed.d --output {args.outputDir}

cli-x64-macos.//: outputDir is the tree this configuration writes: .cache/bin/<platform> by default, dist/bin/<platform> in production (specs/cowshed/06_cli.md, Launcher). One option feeds the declared output, napi's --output-dir and the receipt's --output, so the three cannot name different trees.

options.command: napi build --bin cowshed --target x86_64-apple-darwin --manifest-path crates/cowshed-cli/Cargo.toml --package cowshed-cli --output-dir {args.outputDir} && node "$(realpath ../../node_modules/@smoothbricks/nx-plugin)/../build-inputs/dist/ts/bin/smoo-nx-build-inputs.js" --manifest-path crates/cowshed-cli/Cargo.toml --dep-info x86_64-apple-darwin/debug/cowshed.d --output {args.outputDir}

production.command: napi build --release --bin cowshed --target x86_64-apple-darwin --manifest-path crates/cowshed-cli/Cargo.toml --package cowshed-cli --output-dir {args.outputDir} && node "$(realpath ../../node_modules/@smoothbricks/nx-plugin)/../build-inputs/dist/ts/bin/smoo-nx-build-inputs.js" --manifest-path crates/cowshed-cli/Cargo.toml --dep-info x86_64-apple-darwin/release/cowshed.d --output {args.outputDir}

cli-arm64-linux.//: output is the file this configuration writes: .cache/bin/<platform>/cowshed by default, dist/bin/<platform>/cowshed in production (specs/cowshed/06_cli.md, Launcher). The declared output is its directory, which {options.output}/.. resolves to, so the tree is restored whole and reads the same option the executor writes through.

cli-x64-linux.//: output is the file this configuration writes: .cache/bin/<platform>/cowshed by default, dist/bin/<platform>/cowshed in production (specs/cowshed/06_cli.md, Launcher). The declared output is its directory, which {options.output}/.. resolves to, so the tree is restored whole and reads the same option the executor writes through.

host-napi-test.//: openHost and the typed launchers end to end: the built addon starts the package launcher's cowshed host, and each launcher spawns its verb through the package launcher, so the launcher's binary must be this checkout's build, the cli-native development build under .cache/bin/<platform>. It needs a Mac: host.diskCommand runs the real hdiutil. The root host-e2e aggregate reaches it and gate reaches it through that; test never does, because the Linux CI job runs test (specs/cowshed/08_testing.md, CI).

launcher-test.//: dependsOn ^build so lmao/dist exists: bunfig.napi-test.toml preloads ../../lmao/dist/ts/bun/trace-preload.js, and without the edge a cold cache runs this target before lmao:build.

wire-fixtures.//: The napi wire corpus is DERIVED from cowshed-core's DTOs: regenerating it is a build step with declared inputs, never a recipe an author has to remember after changing a DTO. Runs ahead of cargo-test-build because crates/cowshed-napi includes the file with include_str!, so the corpus has to be current before any test binary compiles it in. The Rust assertion that the committed file equals what core serializes stays as the proof; this target is what keeps it true.

capability-probe.//: rustc's verdict on the cowshed-core capability probe: each file of crates/cowshed-core/tests/capability_probe is a crate that must not compile, and scripts/capability-probe.sh checks them all with one cargo and writes what rustc said of each. public_api_contracts' lesser_capabilities_fail_to_compile_with_coordinator_authority reads that file and judges it, so no test compiles anything: cowshed-core's dependency build takes minutes on a cold runner, and no runner's progress bound is spent on it. Every cowshed-core runner depends on this target and keys on its output (nx.json targetDefaults), because which runner holds the test follows from the plugin's partition of the crate, not from anything declared here. Nx resolves one targetDefaults key per target, the most specific glob, so the cargo-test-cowshed-core-* key restates the apfs-test-root edge of cargo-test-cowshed-*.

capability-probe-test.//: Witness that cowshed:capability-probe publishes a verdict only when rustc answered for every case, exactly the errors rustc located in each case's crate, and leaves no verdict and no staged workspace behind when it refuses. Nx caches what the script wrote and every cowshed-core runner keys on it, so a non-answer published as an answer would fail the test on every run until an input changed. Cargo is faked at its published interface; the real compiler run is the capability-probe target.

declaration-model-test.//: The public declaration IR runs its source lint before the real admission oracle, using the actual prebuilt owner generator and one Typia world. It needs no N-API wire corpus or native runtime fixture. Its typia plugin warmth is the fixture segment below, shared with wire-test.

options.command: biome check --files-ignore-unknown=true declaration-model.test.ts && eslint declaration-model.test.ts && bun test --config=../bunfig.toml --timeout=0 declaration-model.test.ts

wire-test.//: Runs from source under the typia transform because the validators under test are the point. Depends on wire-fixtures (the corpus is a generated output, current by construction) and not on cargo-test: the Rust half proves the same corpus through include_str!, and cowshed:test already joins both legs; a cargo-test edge here only meant an unrelated Rust failure deleted this target from the run. Its typia plugin warmth is the fixture segment below: the first load through the compiler preload compiles the native plugin for minutes on a cold Go cache, in a cache outside Nx outputs, so it runs as this task's build interval under a 600s budget, where a cache hit restores the verdict without warming anything.

lineage-js.//: The process-lineage entry (specs/cowshed/07_api.md section Process lineage) compiled on its own into dist/lineage, apart from tsc-js's dist/ts: its closure is src/process-lineage.ts, src/addon.ts and src/platform.ts, with no generated or typia module, so it depends on no cowshed target and nx-plugin compiles against it without cowshed's whole build. It writes dist/lineage/.build-inputs.json through build-inputs' smoo-nx-build-inputs, its one dependency, naming the files it compiles, so a consumer that links cowshed judges dist/lineage by content (specs/cli/01_workspace_reconciliation.md). A cache miss forces this small program to emit so existing build-info cannot hide a missing public output.

options.command: tsc --build tsconfig.lineage.json --force && node ../build-inputs/dist/ts/bin/smoo-nx-build-inputs.js --input src/process-lineage.ts --input src/addon.ts --input src/platform.ts --input tsconfig.lineage.json --input ../../tsconfig.base.json --output dist/lineage

release-check.//: The package's release gate: smoo release pack runs it in the publishing job after every platform's prebuilt outputs are applied and before the tarball is packed, and refuses a gate that declares dependsOn or is not cached on a runtime digest of the packed bytes, so it judges the bytes that get packed, never a rebuild, and a replay stands for exactly those bytes. It judges the shipping trees under dist/bin and dist/native (the execute bits that survive the artifact round trip, and the addons), and a missing or empty tree fails it: it used to pass by finding nothing. The development builds under .cache/bin are never shipped.

test.//: Replaces the inferred test. cargo-test is the ordinary crate suite alone, reached here through napi-test. The root's host-e2e aggregate owns the serial real-image groups and host-napi-test, and gate reaches them without adding them to ordinary test. They replay from cache unless their own inputs change.

apfs-test-root.//: Makes sure the per-user mount root that real-image fixtures keep their scratch trees below exists, as cowshed setup makes it: /private/var/folders/cowshed, its <uid> directory, and mnt inside that (specs/cowshed/08_testing.md, Integration tests). The fixtures make t themselves, and a cowshed exec sandbox denies it, so it is never touched here. On a host setup has been through it only checks, and changes nothing. The directories are host state, not an Nx output, so the cache key is the --probe runtime input: provisioned on a host with all three as required, and a value of its own run while any is missing, so a fresh runner never replays a skip. It does nothing off macOS. The note is not an option: nx:run-commands forwards every option it does not know to the command as an argument.

apfs-test-root-test.//: Unit tests of apfs-test-root.ts: every decision against an in-memory host, the real lstat and install against a temporary directory, and pins of its paths and modes to the Rust code that makes and refuses them. Runs from the project root on an explicit path, with an empty Bun config: the package bunfig.toml preloads LMAO's compiler and trace hooks, which a script test has no use for and which would make it wait on lmao's build. The host OS is an input because a darwin-only case skips elsewhere, and a result cached there must not replay here.

host-controller-test.//: Run from an unsandboxed host-controller shell, never cowshed exec: controller fixtures require file-link, deliberately denied to every workspace supervisor and child. Runs ignored host_controller_ tests in place from the owning workspace's test build, whose reuse-build metadata is a hashed input. Compilation is cached and paid by cargo-test-build before this run, or by the script's ensure step when that build was a cache hit that restored only the metadata; the private runtime TMPDIR cannot change the compiled environment. The fixtures run the development CLI (cli-native), the compiled TypeScript package (tsc-js) and the host's default Node-API addon (napi-native), which build first.

integration-apfs.//: Cached on the crate closure, the toolchain and the host kernel it exercises. It runs from the workspace root so its first step can sweep dead runs (scripts/apfs-test-sweep.ts, from the root's test build, in place) before its fixtures start; replayed from cache it starts none and sweeps nothing.

benchmark-apfs.//: Cached on the crate closure, the toolchain and the host kernel it exercises.

description: Warm git workspaces: instant isolated copy-on-write workspaces with layered sandboxing (CLI, Rust API, NAPI bindings)
